question: Under the Biomedical Waste Management Rules 2016, used syringes, needles, and scalpels (sharps) must be discarded in which coloured container?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Yellow bags are for human anatomical waste, soiled items, and expired medicines — not sharps. Sharps require a puncture-proof translucent container.
Red bags collect contaminated recyclable items such as tubings and catheters, not sharps. Sharps need a puncture-proof container (white translucent).

Correct. The BMW Rules 2016 specify white translucent puncture-proof containers for sharps (Category 10). These are sealed at 3/4 capacity and sent to the Common Biomedical Waste Treatment Facility (CBWTF).
Blue containers are for glassware and metallic items. Sharps belong in white translucent puncture-proof containers to prevent needle-stick injuries during handling.

overallFeedback.feedback: Sharps require special puncture-proof containment. Review the BMW Rules 2016 colour-code chart: white translucent for sharps (Category 10).
Well done. White translucent puncture-proof containers are mandated for all sharps under Category 10 of the BMW Rules 2016.
